case_title: Pathan Hussain Basha v. State of A.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband of the deceased); mother-in-law of the deceased (Relative: mother-in-law)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B read with s.498-A (Evidence Act s.113-B referred to in judgment)
weapon: None mentioned (death by hanging with a saree)
evidence_type: Eyewitness/oral testimony of relatives and neighbours (LW-1, LW-3, LW-7); medical (post-mortem by LW-13); recovery and seizure of saree; scene photographs
aggravating_circumstances: Persistent dowry demands; victim beaten and abused for dowry; victim refused return to parental home; death within a very short period after marriage
mitigating_circumstances: Age of the accused; substantial period already spent in jail; attendant circumstances
trial_court_outcome: All three accused convicted under ss.304-B and 498-A IPC; life imprisonment under s.304-B; 3 years RI under s.498-A (concurrent); fine Rs 1,000 each
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed: father-in-law acquitted; conviction and sentence of husband and mother-in-law confirmed
offence_finally_established: Dowry death (IPC s.304-B) read with cruelty (IPC s.498-A)
neutral_facts: The victim was married in June 2002 in an arranged marriage. At the marriage, a dowry of Rs 25,000 was promised by the victim's side; Rs 15,000 was paid then and the balance of Rs 10,000 was promised within about four months. The victim's father could not pay the balance. The prosecution alleged that the accused, the victim's spouse and mother-in-law, pressed for the balance, harassed the victim for non-payment, refused to send the victim to the parental home, and that the victim had told relatives about the ill-treatment. A witness said that the couple was happy for the first months and that quarrels followed. On one visit to the parental home, the spouse demanded a fan, a ring and Rs 1,000 in cash, along with the balance dowry; when these were not met, the spouse left the victim there. On 15 February 2003, around 11 a.m., the accused left a witness in the house on an errand. When the witness returned, the victim was found hanging from a beam with a saree. The victim's parents came, cut the victim down and took the victim to hospital, where the victim was declared dead. Police registered the report, seized the saree used for hanging, photographed the scene and arranged a post-mortem. The doctor found an oblique ligature mark on the front and left sides of the neck and an abrasion on the chin, all antemortem, and recorded asphyxia from hanging as the cause of death. The victim's father's account was corroborated by two other witnesses. One witness stated that the dowry of Rs 15,000 was handed over at the marriage and that the balance was not paid. The witnesses described the persistent dowry demands and beating and abuse of the victim.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia from hanging; antemortem oblique ligature mark on neck and abrasion on chin; victim reportedly beaten by accused
financial_property_loss: Rs 15,000 paid at marriage toward Rs 25,000 dowry; balance Rs 10,000 demanded and not paid; other items demanded (fan, ring, Rs 1,000 cash)
motive: Accepted by court: persistent dowry demands (balance of agreed dowry and other items such as fan, ring and Rs 1,000 cash)
key_evidence_accepted: Oral evidence of the victim's father (LW-1), LW-3 and LW-7 on dowry demands and cruelty; victim's reports of ill-treatment to parents; post-mortem findings (LW-13); seizure of saree
witness_credibility: Court found the prosecution evidence reliable and cogent; the witnesses' accounts were consistent and corroborated each other
post_offence_conduct: Did not explain how the death occurred and maintained silence; court held silence and denial do not discharge the onus
custody_duration: Arrested 16 February 2003; in jail for a considerable period (not quantified)
trial_duration: offence: 15 February 2003; trial judgment: 4 October 2004; High Court: 26 October 2006; Supreme Court: 16 August 2012
legal_representation: Appellants: Param Kumar Mishra (for Kumud Lata Das); State: D. Mahesh Babu
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation conducted and post-mortem done; accused arrested 16 February 2003; committed to Sessions Court; tried
appeal_history: Trial court: all three convicted (ss.304-B, 498-A), life imprisonment; High Court: father-in-law acquitted, husband and mother-in-law convicted and sentence confirmed; Supreme Court: convictions upheld, sentence reduced to ten years RI
prosecution_argument: Not stated; the judgment records no State submissions beyond noting that the State did not challenge the father-in-law's acquittal
defence_argument: Sought lenient view on sentence given the age of the accused, the attendant circumstances, and the time already spent in jail
legal_principle_applied: Under s.304-B read with s.113-B Evidence Act, once basic ingredients are proved the accused must show the death was not caused by cruelty or dowry demand; denial or silence does not discharge the onus
precedent_relied_upon: Biswajit Halder v. State of W.B. (2008) 1 SCC 202 and Ashok Kumar v. State of Haryana (2010) 12 SCC 350 (relied on); also discussed: Tarsem Singh (2008) 16 SCC 155, Yashoda v. State of M.P. (2004) 3 SCC 98, Ran Singh (2008) 4 SCC 700, Satvir Singh (2001) 8 SCC 633, State of A.P. v. Raj Gopal Asawa (2004) 4 SCC 470
sentencing_rationale: Lenient view taken given the prosecution evidence, attendant circumstances, age of the accused and time already in jail; ends of justice met by reducing sentence to ten years RI
judicial_mitigating_factors: Age of the accused; substantial period already spent in jail; attendant circumstances
judicial_aggravating_factors: None expressly weighed; court noted as established the persistent dowry demands and beating and abuse of the victim
